QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_18

question.text: A SAS-200 drinking-water programme under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) co-funding needs the SIA to handle dual attribution. The MOST appropriate indicator for the NPO-specific contribution is:

answer.text: Number of Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC) in the village — pure JJM indicator
Total households in the village including those never served
Incremental households with safe drinking water attributable to the NPO's overhead-tank / filtration-plant work, net of FHTC coverage

explanation.text: The Logic: When a government scheme co-funds a programme, the SIA must isolate the incremental households served by the NPO's specific work — here, overhead-tank and filtration-plant infrastructure — over and above the government scheme's baseline coverage. Reporting only the gross figure would conflate two attribution sources and overstate the NPO's contribution. The Trap: Option A reports pure JJM/FHTC figures and double-counts. Option B is a denominator, not an attribution indicator. Option D uses a state-average benchmark, which is a reference point rather than an attribution measure. Note: The specific Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) / FHTC co-funding scenario and the net-of-FHTC attribution rule are not described in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) pages 31, 55, 117, 186 or 192-193. The overhead-tank / filtration-plant facts belong to the SAS-1100 Swagruha Niwas case rather than a SAS-200 JJM case. The framing above reflects general industry knowledge of attribution in co-funded interventions.
